title: Optimization in Higher Dimensions: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Optimization in Higher Dimensions: Visual Guide

1. Gradient To Step | the familiar gradient vector on the contours of J = x^2 + 3y^2, drawn as an uphill arrow whose length is the largest directional derivative, next to the new arrow -alpha*grad J that this lesson adds, with the point and the learning rate both draggable | the gradient supplies the DIRECTION and alpha supplies the DISTANCE; new point = old point - alpha * gradient, and the gradient must be re-evaluated at the new point every step

2. Why Squares Not Signs | three data points and a line y = mx + b with every residual drawn signed, the signed total and the squared total side by side, preset lines and live gradient-descent steps on m and b | positive and negative errors cancel so the signed total calls a terrible line perfect, which is why least squares squares; and it is m and b that get updated, never the data x_i, y_i or n

3. The Learning Rate Dial | J = a*theta^2 reduced to theta <- (1 - 2*a*alpha)*theta, with the iterates drawn on the parabola and a per-iteration cost bar chart, plus a curvature slider | too small = slow monotone, too large = overshooting oscillation that still trends down, |factor| >= 1 = divergence; the safe window is 1/a, so the same alpha changes verdict when the curvature changes

4. Valleys And Restarts | descent on the double well f = x^4 - 4x^2 + 0.5x from a draggable start, plus a restart-from-12-random-points mode scoring how many found the deeper valley | gradient descent is a local rule and can get trapped in a local minimum, two starts may settle in different minima, and random restarts improve the odds without ever guaranteeing the global minimum

5. Newton Versus Descent | the parabola model q(x) fitted at the start point with its vertex marked as the first Newton step, an iteration table against gradient descent, and a shape check for the multivariable product | x - g'(x)/g''(x) reaches a near-exact answer in a few iterations because it uses curvature, but it solves g' = 0 and so converges to maxima too; in n dimensions the Hessian replaces g'' and only H^-1 * grad g has valid shapes
